title: Cultural Dimensions of Artificial Intelligence Adoption: Empirical Insights for Wave 1 from a Multinational Longitudinal Pilot Study

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying multinational participants using Likert-scale items and qualitative self-assessments to evaluate their perceptions of AI's cultural sensitivity, specifically whether AI outputs reflect culture-specific orientations and how cultural values impact trust and adoption.

Collecting self-reported survey responses to assess the perceived influence of language on AI interactions, focusing on disparities in effectiveness between native and non-native language usage, as well as the impact of field-specific or academic jargon.
Using cross-tabulations and Chi-square statistical testing on survey data to evaluate significant disparities in AI adoption, reliance, and usage purposes across different age groups.
Administering surveys to measure participants' perceptions of whether gender plays a role in influencing AI engagement and usage patterns.
Administering surveys to evaluate participant perceptions regarding the extent to which religious orientations influence interactions with and adoption of AI.
